name: Kitbag
description: A single-file H5 baggage planner. The world is capacity under two opposed constraints and a charge that jumps rather than scales: each bag has an allowance, going over costs £45 up to 3 kg, £75 up to 8 kg and £120 beyond, so 260 g over costs exactly what 2.9 kg over costs. On top sit placement rules that pull the other way — anything with a battery must fly in the cabin, liquids over 100 ml and anything sharp must go in the hold — and two paid extras whose value depends entirely on which bag is actually the binding one. 6 screens, 3 bags, 20 items, 4 rules, 3 fee bands.

finish.answer: final answer for question tasks; optional for action tasks

observation.text: engine.a11y(state) — every bag prints its weight, its allowance, how far over it is and which fee band that lands in, so the whole optimisation is legible without pixels.
observation.pixels: 390x844 screenshot (browser backend); __ENV__.bounds() maps every test-id to a pixel box
observation.state: engine.snapshot(state) — canonical state plus a derived view keyed by item and bag name. For the verifier only.

world.weight: every weight is an integer in grams; money is an integer in pence
world.allowances: hold 15 kg, cabin 7 kg, an optional second hold bag 15 kg for £50
world.bands: excess is charged per bag by band, not by weight: £45 up to 3 kg over, £75 up to 8 kg, £120 beyond
world.rules: battery → cabin only; liquid over 100 ml → hold only; sharp → hold only; oversized → hold only
world.priority: priority boarding costs £12 and adds 2 kg to the cabin allowance — worth it only when the cabin is the binding bag
world.seeded: the hold starts 2.36 kg over with the laptop and the power bank illegally in it; fixing only the rules leaves it 260 g over and the fee unchanged
world.totals: the twenty items weigh 19.9 kg against 22 kg of allowance, so a zero-charge packing exists
